activityGoals.name: Seconds to Minutes Conversion
activityGoals.goalDescription: Construct a program that obtains minutes and remaining seconds from the input amount of time in seconds. For example, 500 seconds contains 8 minutes and 20 seconds.
activityGoals.correctOutput:
Enter an integer for seconds: 
450 seconds is 7 minutes and 30 seconds.

commentList: We need to read and process the value that the user enters. To read the input value from the user, we need to define a Scanner object.

We can create a Scanner object using the operator new, as shown in this statement. The System.in object represents the standard input stream, which by default is the keyboard. It tells the java compiler that the input will be provided through keyboard.
We prompt the user to enter the seconds.
We need to read the seconds that the user enters and store it in a variable. We read the seconds by calling the nextInt() method because this input is an integer.
Note that if the user provides a non-integer number, an exception will be thrown because the input type is inconsistent with the expected data type, i.e., int.
We close the scanner as we do not want to process any input from the user in the rest of the program.

lineList.content: //Step 2: Obtain minutes and remaining seconds from the input seconds

commentList: To obtain the minutes in seconds, we divide the seconds by 60 because there are 60 seconds in a minute. Note that since both operands of division operator are integer, the fractional part of the result is truncated, if there is any.

To obtain the remaining seconds after taking away the minutes, we have to take the remainder of the seconds divided by 60. This is because there are 60 seconds in a minute. Note that the % operator returns the remainder of the division.

lineList.content: System.out.println(seconds + " seconds is " + minutes +    " minutes and " + remainingSeconds + " seconds.");

activityGoals.name: Converting Milliseconds to Hours, Minutes, and Seconds
activityGoals.goalDescription: Construct a program that obtains hours, minutes, and seconds from an amount of time in milliseconds.
activityGoals.correctOutput:
Enter the milliseconds: 
16803000 milliseconds is 4 hours and 40 minutes and 3 seconds.

commentList: We need to read and process the value that the user enters. To read the input value from the user, we need to define a Scanner object.

We can create a Scanner object using the operator new, as shown in this statement. The System.in object represents the standard input stream, which by default is the keyboard. It tells the java compiler that the input will be provided through keyboard.
We prompt the user to enter the milliseconds.

We need to read the milliseconds that the user enters and store it in a variable. We read the milliseconds by calling the nextLong() method because this input could be a large integer. Therefore, we need to define the variable totalMilliseconds as long because it could hold integer numbers that are too large to fit in the int data type.
Note that if the user provides a number that could not be converted to long, an exception will be thrown because the input type is inconsistent with the expected data type, i.e., long.
We close the scanner as we do not want to process any input from the user in the rest of the program.

lineList.content: //Step 2: Obtain hours, minutes and seconds from the milliseconds

commentList: To obtain the total seconds in milliseconds, we divide the milliseconds by 1000 because there are 1000 milliseconds in a second. Note that since the operands of division operator are long and integer, the fractional part of the result is truncated, if there is any.

To obtain the hours, we divide the seconds by 3600 because there are 3600 seconds in an hour. Note that since the operands of division operator are long and integer, the fractional part of the result is truncated, if there is any.

To obtain the remaining minutes after taking away the hours, we have to take the remainder of the total minutes divided by 60. We get the total minutes by dividing the seconds by 60. The % operator returns the remainder of the division.
Note that since the operands of division operator are long and integer, the fractional part of the result is truncated, if there is any.
To obtain the remaining seconds after taking away the minutes, we have to take the remainder of the total seconds divided by 60. Note that the % operator returns the remainder of the division.

lineList.content: System.out.println(milliSeconds+" milliseconds is "+hours + " hours and " + mins + " minutes and " + secs + " seconds.");
commentList: This statement prints to the default standard output stream the hours, minutes, and seconds from the input amount of time in milliseconds. The printed text is followed by the end-of-line character at the end.
The expression in the argument of the println method returns a string that is obtained by concatenating the given strings and value of the variables.
